answer: Before the season the wardens bury a beacon at each marked spot and log its signal, so a buried beacon can be found by its own pulse. A lagoon beacon bought at a shop fails the registry: at the horizon of the burial the signal must match the warden's own log, and a shop beacon pulses with another code. Faking a registry means burying forty beacons across the valley, hiring wardens and paying 18,200, while the fable entry in the rescue office is read at every search, so a beacon whose burial was never logged is ignored.
